name: Craigslist
tagline: Regional classifieds for jobs, housing, gigs, and used stuff, in HTML from another decade.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Most categories are free to post, some (job ads, brokered apartments, dealer vehicles) carry a per-post fee that varies by city.

verdictSummary: The software here is trivially replicable: a posting form, a category tree, a city selector, and search. That has never been the point. Craigslist is valuable because when you list a couch in your metro, actual local humans see it within an hour, and that is thirty years of accumulated habit in thousands of local markets. A self-hosted classifieds board with one user is a diary. The closest honest build is not a competitor, it is a client: something that watches Craigslist for you and pings you first.
coreLoopDIY: Polls Craigslist search RSS feeds for your saved queries across chosen cities, dedupes results into SQLite, and notifies you on new matches.
requirements: Node runtime and a place to run a cron job
Craigslist search RSS URLs for the cities and categories you care about
Optional: an ntfy topic or Telegram bot token for push alerts
whatYouLose: Buyers and sellers, which is the entire product
Local liquidity: a listing that reaches your actual metro within minutes
Anti-scam scale: flagging, ghosting, and pattern detection built on enormous traffic
Category depth in housing, jobs, and gigs that nobody else covers in mid-size cities
Being the default place people already check without being told
moatNotes: The ugliest site on the internet keeps winning because everyone in your zip code already knows where it is.
whyPeopleStillPay: Mostly they do not pay, which makes the moat even more annoying to attack. Where money changes hands (job postings, brokered apartment listings, dealer vehicles) people pay because a single posting reaches the exact local audience that would otherwise cost hundreds in ads to assemble. The fee is a filter, not a feature: it prices out spam while the free categories keep the traffic flowing. No amount of better software moves that audience.
notes: You can build the board in an afternoon and it will sit empty forever. The moat is marketplace liquidity: decades of local habit in thousands of metros, which no self-hosted instance inherits.
prompt:
Build a local-only Craigslist watcher CLI called "clwatch". Do not build a classifieds marketplace, build a monitoring client.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with TypeScript, run via tsx
- SQLite through better-sqlite3, file at ./data/clwatch.db
- rss-parser for feeds, undici for any raw fetch
- commander for the CLI
- No web server, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud

How it works:
- Craigslist search result pages expose an RSS feed. The user supplies full feed URLs (for example a search URL with format=rss) via `clwatch add`.
- Schema: watches(id, label, feed_url, min_price, max_price, include_keywords, exclude_keywords, active, created_at) and listings(id, watch_id, guid, title, url, price, location, posted_at, first_seen_at, notified_at, hidden).
- `clwatch add --label "cheap desks" --url "..." --max-price 150 --exclude "ikea,broken"` creates a watch.
- `clwatch poll` fetches every active watch sequentially with a 3 to 6 second randomized delay between requests, a plain descriptive User-Agent from .env, and 3 retries with exponential backoff. Parse title, link, price if present in the title, and location. Insert only unseen guids.
- Filtering: drop items outside the price range or matching exclude keywords, require all include keywords if given.
- Notifications: if NTFY_TOPIC is set in .env, POST new matches to ntfy.sh. Otherwise print them. Mark notified_at so nothing repeats.
- `clwatch list` shows watches with match counts. `clwatch recent --limit 20` prints newest unhidden matches as a table with clickable URLs. `clwatch hide <id>` buries one.
- Store all timestamps UTC ISO 8601.

Also do:
- .env.example with USER_AGENT and NTFY_TOPIC, plus .env in .gitignore
- A README with one crontab line for polling every 15 minutes and a blunt note that polling too fast will get the IP blocked
- Seed script that adds two example watches so `poll` can be tested immediately

Explicitly out of scope: posting listings, messaging sellers, scraping listing bodies or images, logging into Craigslist, any hosted UI.
